Subject: On-prem preflight and inventory for Redwood private deployment

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We want to get an internal preflight in motion so we can sign the PO and schedule a pilot rack with our field ops team. Two asks to start: 1) a concise recommended node-pool & storage architecture that aligns with our mix of ML inference (mostly low-latency text gen) and batch embedding jobs, and 2) a minimal network egress/NAT pattern that satisfies our security team.

Context: we'll be colocating in our primary DC (rack A12). Target cluster size to start: 8-12 worker nodes; we can expand after pilot. We have a mix of NVIDIA A40s and a pool of standard cpu-only servers for control-plane and lighter workloads. Storage: local NVMe per node (boot+scratch) and a backend SAN (iSCSI) for durable volumes.

Can you confirm what you need from us to validate node types, PV profiles, and whether we should plan for a Ceph/Rook deployment or rely on SAN-backed PVs? Also, what port/IPs should our network team expect to open for health checks, telemetry, and the private control plane?

I'll attach our site inventory (stub) — ops-infra can fill gaps.

Thanks,
Derek Hale
Head of Infrastructure
Acme Health Systems

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: On-prem preflight and inventory for Redwood private deployment

Hi Derek —

Appreciate the context. Summary answer up front: for your workload mix we recommend a three-ring node strategy plus a lightweight durable storage layer (Rook/Ceph recommended if you expect >2x scaling in 6-12 months; SAN-backed PVs are acceptable for pilot). Network: plan for an outbound NAT range for model fetches + telemetry and two dedicated egress IPs for callbacks; we provide a short ACL list below.

High-level node pools (pilot):
- control-plane (3 x cpu-highmem, 32GB+ RAM, no GPU) — kubeadm control plane, etcd, control-plane-level observability (separate from customer workloads).
- infer-gpu (2-4 x A40/A100 class GPUs depending on throughput target; we suggest heterogeneous labels: gpu-high (A100 x2 pods), gpu-standard (A40 single pod) so we can route by latency vs cost).
- worker-cpu (3-4 x cpu-only nodes for batch embeddings, offline jobs, sidecars).

Storage recommendations:
- local NVMe: use for ephemeral KV cache (fast cache PVs, HostPath or LocalPV with topology aware provisioning). Use reclaim policy: Delete for cache volumes.
- durable volumes: prefer Rook/Ceph (replicated block) if you plan persistent model shards across reboots and want self-healing. Rook requirements: min 3 OSD nodes (we can use 3 worker-cpu nodes or three dedicated disk nodes). Ceph tuning: use bluestore, 32k pg settings, and ensure 10Gbps between OSDs.
- SAN-backed PVs (iSCSI/Fibre): acceptable for pilot if you set StorageClass with WaitForFirstConsumer and enable dynamic resizing and ioProfiles. Plan for at least 2000 IOPS per model shard PV if you expect concurrent token rates.

Network / egress & services:
- Outbound: allow ports 443 to our telemetry and model catalog endpoints; whitelist two static egress IPs we'll provide once dedicated capacity is provisioned.
- Inbound: load balancer (metalLB BGP mode recommended) to expose inference endpoints; ensure health-check ports 8080/9000 open from LB to node ports.
- Control-plane access: restrict kubectl/API server access to your admin CIDR + our ops bastion (we can provide a short-lived cert for initial bootstrap).

Preflight checklist items we need from you:
1) Completed site inventory (attached).
2) Network topology diagram + firewall ACLs.
3) Expected concurrency (qps, average tokens per request) for both interactive and batch.
4) Confirm SAN vs Ceph decision for pilot.

I've attached our preflight checklist template; happy to fill it in during a short working session. I cc'd Marissa and Ben for commercial/ops alignment (disk sizing and reserved capacity notes).

Best,
Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: preflight-checklist-template.xlsx (template)

Subject: Re: Preflight: on-prem cluster assessment — node pools, storage, and network QA

Looping in commercial details — quick notes:
- If Acme elects SAN-backed pilot (no durable distributed storage), we should mark the engagement as a 3-month pilot with no guaranteed SLA on durability until we onboard Rook/Ceph.
- For dedicated GPU nodes (if they want A100s reserved) we should propose a small reserved capacity commitment to cover the expected steady QPS.
- Ben, please add recommended compression/quantization guidance to reduce PV sizes if the customer is constrained on SAN capacity.

Marissa
VP, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 08:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: on-prem cluster assessment — node pools, storage, and network QA

Quick technical add:
- If Acme wants to start with SAN-backed PVs, recommend we provision PVs with default fsType=ext4 and mount options=noatime,nodiratime; enable io-queueing on controller.
- For model artifacts, consider gzip or fp16 quantization to cut PV footprint 2-4x; we can provide a conversion pipeline as part of onboarding.
- Local NVMe should be used for token cache with an LRU eviction policy; we typically size cache as 5-10% of total model artifacts if latency-critical.

I can draft the minimal helm values we'd recommend for the Rook deployment (if they go that route).

—Ben
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
